page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-128GB is a memory-dense cloud virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 9575F processors running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation totals 128.0 GB of RAM, delivering a 16.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Storage is configured with 400 GB of integrated SSD capacity, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show exceptional single-thread compute capabilities alongside moderate memory throughput. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng and Geekbench 6, place the instance in the top tier with scores of 3536.19 and 2299.0 respectively. Single-threaded data compression also achieves top-tier results, reaching 38.45 GB/sec in gzip. Conversely, uncached large-block memory write bandwidth drops to 15.87 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% of tested configurations. Multi-threaded CPU execution and Redis SET operations deliver typical middle-tier performance, with Redis processing 9.14 million operations per second.

Because of the 1:16 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and top-tier single-core instruction processing, this server provides high resource density for memory-bound systems that do not require massive parallel thread counts. The bundled 400 GB SSD offers local scratch space, though write-intensive memory pipelines may encounter bandwidth limitations. Recommended workloads include in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached instances, enterprise caching layers, intermediate ETL pipelines, and memory-heavy web applications.
